en.title: GTAVI: An exclusive deep dive into the video game of the decade
en.description: This story is taken from the autumn 2026 issue of Dazed, which is on sale internationally from September 10. Pre-order a copy of the magazine here.
en.fullContent:
This story is taken from the autumn 2026 issue of Dazed, which is on sale internationally from September 10. Pre-order a copy of the magazine here.

On the sweltering Leonida Keys, sweat slicks the skin of two lovers on the run as they toast new beginnings, watching the sun set over the water. A breeze blows through their hair, and you can almost feel the condensation dripping from the cold beer bottles in their hands; in the background, locals gather on the weatherbeaten dock, indifferent to the story unfolding between the outlaws. Elsewhere, a few miles north, tanned bodies of all shapes and sizes swarm the sand on Vice Beach. Further north still, locals are caked in mud, kicked up from the back of a dirt bike or spattered on a stars-and-stripes bikini. And as night falls back in Vice City, sweaty crowds surge to deafening hip-hop beats, spilling out from clubs on to the neon-lit streets.

It’s been 13 years since Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto V, one of the most acclaimed – and controversial – video games of all time. And it’s been roughly the same amount of time since work began on its sequel, Grand Theft Auto VI, which transports the action from San Andreas (closely inspired by real-life southern California) to Leonida (based on Florida). That’s more than a decade of anticipation, meaning there’s “unprecedented pressure” on the follow-up to meet expectations, as Rob Nelson, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, tells Dazed: “However, I don’t know that any amount of external pressure could compare with the pressure we put on ourselves as a team.”

If you accept that video games are an artform, then Rockstar Games has produced two of the most significant works of the 21st century so far: GTAV and the western-themed adventure Red Dead Redemption 2. The numbers speak for themselves: in 2013, the former broke the record for the fastest-selling entertainment product of all time, earning a billion dollars in just three days – more than any book or Hollywood film. Five years later, RDR2 took the second spot. But the latter also came with a gear shift. While GTA satirised modern life with wacky characters, high-octane car chases and explosive gunfights, RDR2 was hailed as one of the most realistic and immersive games to date, with a slower, more emotional tone suited to its storyline.

GTAVI promises something in between the two. The open-world game is set in the same fictionalised US that serves as the backdrop for the rest of the series, with all the weapons and supercars you’d expect, but the world is more grounded and reactive than before – gone are the days when you could traverse the city like a god. Now, players’ actions have consequences. Walk down the street with a rifle, and the city will have something to say about it. More and more, the games are converging on real life, and non-player characters (NPCs) are acting... well, less like NPCs than ever. For some gamers, there’s a fear that what GTAVI gains in immersion, it loses in the chaos and anarchy that have been part of the series’ DNA since the outset, but for Rockstar, the goal is to create a world of total immersion, which reacts more realistically than ever to what you choose to make of it.

“We look back at our previous games with a critical eye and see where we want to evolve based on what we didn’t do as well as we would have liked to, either because we didn’t have the time, resources or technological capabilities, or in some cases things we just didn’t do as well or consider as fully as we could have,” says Nelson. “A lot of what we do is very iterative – we adjust a lot of things by feel based on what is working and what isn’t.”

en.title: GTA 6 Cyberleek update: Everything leaked so far, what might be coming next
en.description: Over the past week or so, someone (or perhaps a group of people) called Cyberleek has been very busy sharing short gameplay clips of Grand Theft Au...
en.fullContent:
Over the past week or so, someone (or perhaps a group of people) called Cyberleek has been very busy sharing short gameplay clips of Grand Theft Auto 6. On Aug. 20, Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of GTA-maker Rockstar Games, filed subpoenas against Microsoft and Discord to try to unmask the leaker, followed soon after by subpoenas against Google and X Corp. Those filings specifically cited "stolen content," seemingly confirming that at least some of the Cyberleek videos are legitimate.

Prior to Thursday's "Extended Look" on Netflix, the GTA 6 leaks represented the first real glimpse of gameplay from the hotly anticipated title. In addition, countless AI-generated videos posing as "leaks" have been circulating widely on social media. So, we've put together a quick list of everything Cyberleek released before seemingly throwing in the towel. We're not going to embed or link to any of these clips; however, they're easy enough to find on X or Reddit if you look hard enough.

At the time of publication, 16 gameplay clips and three map screenshots have been posted by Cyberleek that show different aspects of GTA 6, including glimpses of cutscenes. The leaker did post some minor story spoilers in the most recent release, so be careful if you want to avoid them.

Guess what Apple will release in September in our Big Guessing Game: Apple edition. Enter now for a chance to win an Apple Watch!

Map sneak peek 1: A small, cropped portion of the in-game world map, showing a location called Dalton Island.

Map sneak peek 2: Another cropped portion of the map showing locations called Tequesta Retreat, Gloriana Key, and Catalan Key.

es.fullContent:
Durante la última semana, alguien (o quizás un grupo de personas) llamado Cyberleek ha estado muy ocupado compartiendo breves clips de juego de Grand Theft Auto 6. El 20 de agosto, Take-Two Interactive, la empresa matriz de Rockstar Games, fabricante de GTA, presentó citaciones contra Microsoft y Discord para intentar desenmascarar al filtrador, seguidas poco después por citaciones contra Google y X Corp. Esas presentaciones citaban específicamente "contenido robado", aparentemente confirmando que al menos parte del Los vídeos de Cyberleek son legítimos.

Antes del "Extended Look" del jueves en Netflix, las filtraciones de GTA 6 representaron el primer vistazo real de la jugabilidad del tan esperado título. Además, en las redes sociales han circulado ampliamente innumerables vídeos generados por IA que se hacen pasar por "filtraciones". Entonces, hemos elaborado una lista rápida de todo lo que Cyberleek lanzó antes de tirar la toalla. No vamos a incrustar ni vincular ninguno de estos clips; sin embargo, son bastante fáciles de encontrar en X o Reddit si buscas lo suficiente.

En el momento de la publicación, Cyberleek ha publicado 16 clips de juego y tres capturas de pantalla de mapas que muestran diferentes aspectos de GTA 6, incluidos destellos de escenas. El filtrador publicó algunos spoilers menores de la historia en la versión más reciente, así que tenga cuidado si quiere evitarlos.

Adivina qué lanzará Apple en septiembre en nuestro Big Guessing Game: edición Apple. ¡Participe ahora para tener la oportunidad de ganar un Apple Watch!

en.title: Wow: GTA 6's first gameplay has redefined what videogames are capable of
en.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 ‘Extended Look’ shows off the best looking game ever made
en.fullContent:
Grand Theft Auto 6 ‘Extended Look’ shows off the best looking game ever made

You have to feel sorry for anyone else making a videogame right now. The 27 minute long Grand Theft Auto 6 ‘Extended Look’ is now available to watch on YouTube and Rockstar’s website after its Netflix debut and, after 13 years of development and a virtually unlimited budget, frankly, it makes every other videogame ever made look like it was cobbled together with spit and chicken wire.

What's so staggering at first glance is the sheer level of graphical detail. Every environment looks lived in, every interior is authentically cluttered and every character uniquely realistic in a way that is usually reserved for actual evolutionary biology. Vice City, the game’s Miami analogue, is utterly convincing too, whether viewed from the lofty vantage point of a rooftop bar or down at street level.

What the Extended Look really served to do, though, was give us a better sense of the dual playable protagonists Jason and Lucia, and their relationship. This is a proper Bonnie and Clyde love story, so long as you choose to nurture it. The pair’s relationship has to be maintained with small gestures, as small as pressing a button to hold hands, and apparently while it doesn't factor into how effectively you can rob a bank or hold up a gas station, it will shape how the story plays out.

The whole thing appears to be a more grown up and serious take on the fan favourite Grand Theft Auto formula. A bit like Red Dead Redemption 2, characters move with more weight and momentum and there are more ways to interact with the world around you, rather than just sprinting to the next shootout like a man-shaped mobile weapons platform.

Of course it wouldn't be Grand Theft Auto without a bit of auto, and thankfully the cars were well represented. Based on the footage, Lucia appears to be the ‘wheelman’ of the pair and car chases will be as much about hiding in alleyways like Ryan Gosling in Drive, as they are haring through traffic at 100mph.

es.title: Vaya: el primer gameplay de GTA 6 ha redefinido lo que son capaces de hacer los videojuegos
es.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 'Extended Look' muestra el juego más atractivo jamás creado
es.fullContent:
Grand Theft Auto 6 'Extended Look' muestra el juego más atractivo jamás creado

Tienes que sentir lástima por cualquiera que esté haciendo un videojuego en este momento. Grand Theft Auto 6 'Extended Look', de 27 minutos de duración, ya está disponible para verlo en YouTube y en el sitio web de Rockstar después de su debut en Netflix y, después de 13 años de desarrollo y un presupuesto prácticamente ilimitado, francamente, hace que todos los demás videojuegos jamás creados parezcan improvisados ​​con saliva y alambre de gallinero.

Lo que sorprende a primera vista es el gran nivel de detalle gráfico. Cada entorno parece vivido, cada interior está auténticamente desordenado y cada personaje es excepcionalmente realista de una manera que normalmente está reservada a la biología evolutiva real. Vice City, el análogo del juego en Miami, también es absolutamente convincente, ya sea visto desde el elevado punto de vista de un bar en la azotea o desde el nivel de la calle.

Sin embargo, lo que realmente sirvió para hacer la mirada extendida fue darnos una mejor idea de los dos protagonistas jugables Jason y Lucia, y su relación. Esta es una verdadera historia de amor de Bonnie y Clyde, siempre y cuando elijas cultivarla. La relación de la pareja debe mantenerse con pequeños gestos, tan pequeños como presionar un botón para tomarse de la mano, y aparentemente, si bien no influye en la eficacia con la que se puede robar un banco o asaltar una gasolinera, determinará cómo se desarrolla la historia.

Todo parece ser una versión más adulta y seria de la fórmula favorita de los fanáticos de Grand Theft Auto. Un poco como Red Dead Redemption 2, los personajes se mueven con más peso e impulso y hay más formas de interactuar con el mundo que te rodea, en lugar de simplemente correr hacia el siguiente tiroteo como una plataforma de armas móvil con forma de hombre.

Por supuesto, no sería Grand Theft Auto sin un poco de automóvil y, afortunadamente, los coches estaban bien representados. Según las imágenes, Lucía parece ser el "timonel" de la pareja y las persecuciones de autos se tratarán tanto de esconderse en callejones como Ryan Gosling en Drive, como de atravesar el tráfico a 100 mph.

en.title: The Video Games You Should Play This Weekend – August 28, 2026
en.description: I am relieved that it's finally time for the weekend, because I desperately need to unwind on the couch with some video games. It's been an excitin...
en.fullContent:
I am relieved that it's finally time for the weekend, because I desperately need to unwind on the couch with some video games. It's been an exciting (but very busy) week over here at Game Informer. We finally launched international print subscriptions, meaning you can get physical issues of our magazine in 40 new countries. We also launched a Game Informer app on iOS and Android, and we've got plans for updates over the coming weeks to add new features and smooth out any rough edges. Yesterday, Rockstar revealed the first official look at Grand Theft Auto VI, and it's shaping up to be as huge as we expected. But most of all, it's the week of Gamescom: most of our editorial team is overseas in Germany running the official Game Informer booths, mingling with games industry folks from around the world, and taking lots of appointments to see games. We saw The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Songs of the Past, Control Resonant, and more: you can see the whole rundown of our most notable demos here.

It's a lot, but luckily for us, there's an easy solution for the fatigue of a busy work week: video games. Here's what you should be playing this weekend.

The simplest way to explain Blood Dungeon is "Vampire Survivors with jumping," though that's a bit reductive. This roguelike bullet heaven adds platforming into the genre's signature power crawl, and has you hop your way through the chaotic titular dungeon. That said, it's definitely a bit of an acquired taste – the art style is intentionally crude, and our reviewer Kyle Hilliard didn't love that, for example, he couldn't get a fart cloud upgrade without hearing a barrage of flatulent sounds during his run. Still, for some of you, details like that are all you need to pull the trigger and pick the game up, so to each their own.

Blood Dungeon is clearly born from Vampire Survivors’ undeniable loop and sense of progression, but developer Messhof addresses arguably the primary shortcoming of the 2022 Bullet Heaven game (I think that’s what we’ve agreed to call these, right?): movement. Moving in Blood Dungeon is fun and it sets the game apart within the genre and demands enjoyable skill from the player, but some balance annoyances keep the game from soaring.

"XCOM meets Star Wars" is such a solid premise that I knew I'd be sold on Zero Company from the moment it was announced, and now that I've started playing it, it's everything I hoped it would be. It's set during the Clone Wars (between Attack of the Clones and Revenge of the Sith) and follows a ragtag group of fighters as they track down a dangerous cult called The Coil. Our reviewer, guest contributor James Galizio, didn't love the story, but said the excellent tactics gameplay mostly makes up for the narrative faults.

Developer Bit Reactor largely succeeds at what it sets out to do, and if you’re a fan of either Star Wars or XCOM it’s an easy recommendation, even if I wish the story had just a bit more juice. If you’re looking for a sci-fi tactics fix, Zero Company delivers the goods.

es.title: Los videojuegos que deberías jugar este fin de semana – 28 de agosto de 2026
es.description: Me siento aliviado de que finalmente haya llegado el fin de semana, porque necesito desesperadamente relajarme en el sofá con algunos videojuegos. ...
es.fullContent:
Me siento aliviado de que finalmente haya llegado el fin de semana, porque necesito desesperadamente relajarme en el sofá con algunos videojuegos. Ha sido una semana emocionante (pero muy ocupada) aquí en Game Informer. Finalmente lanzamos suscripciones impresas internacionales, lo que significa que puede obtener números físicos de nuestra revista en 40 nuevos países. También lanzamos una aplicación Game Informer en iOS y Android, y tenemos planes de actualizaciones durante las próximas semanas para agregar nuevas funciones y suavizar cualquier aspereza. Ayer, Rockstar reveló el primer vistazo oficial a Grand Theft Auto VI, y se perfila como tan grande como esperábamos. Pero, sobre todo, es la semana de Gamescom: la mayor parte de nuestro equipo editorial se encuentra en Alemania, gestionando los stands oficiales de Game Informer, interactuando con gente de la industria de los juegos de todo el mundo y asistiendo a muchas citas para ver juegos. Vimos The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Songs of the Past, Control Resonant y más: puedes ver el resumen completo de nuestras demostraciones más destacadas aquí.

Es mucho, pero afortunadamente para nosotros, existe una solución fácil para el cansancio de una semana laboral ocupada: los videojuegos. Esto es lo que deberías jugar este fin de semana.

La forma más sencilla de explicar Blood Dungeon es "Vampire Survivors con saltos", aunque es un poco reduccionista. Este paraíso de balas roguelike agrega plataformas al poder característico del género y te permite abrirte camino a través de la caótica mazmorra titular. Dicho esto, definitivamente es un gusto adquirido: el estilo artístico es intencionalmente crudo, y a nuestro crítico Kyle Hilliard no le gustó que, por ejemplo, no pudiera actualizar una nube de pedos sin escuchar un aluvión de sonidos flatulentos durante su carrera. Aún así, para algunos de ustedes, detalles como ese son todo lo que necesitan para apretar el gatillo y retomar el juego, cada uno con lo suyo.

Blood Dungeon nace claramente del innegable bucle y sentido de progresión de Vampire Survivors, pero el desarrollador Messhof aborda posiblemente la principal deficiencia del juego Bullet Heaven 2022 (creo que así es como acordamos llamarlos, ¿verdad?): movimiento. Moverse en Blood Dungeon es divertido y distingue al juego dentro del género y exige una habilidad agradable por parte del jugador, pero algunas molestias en el equilibrio impiden que el juego se dispare.

"XCOM se encuentra con Star Wars" es una premisa tan sólida que supe que Zero Company me vendería desde el momento en que se anunció, y ahora que comencé a jugarlo, es todo lo que esperaba que fuera. Está ambientado durante las Guerras Clon (entre El Ataque de los Clones y La Venganza de los Sith) y sigue a un grupo heterogéneo de luchadores mientras rastrean una secta peligrosa llamada The Coil. A nuestro crítico, el colaborador invitado James Galizio, no le encantó la historia, pero dijo que la excelente jugabilidad táctica compensa en gran medida las fallas narrativas.

El desarrollador Bit Reactor tiene gran éxito en lo que se propone hacer, y si eres fanático de Star Wars o XCOM, es una recomendación fácil, incluso si desearía que la historia tuviera un poco más de jugo. Si está buscando una solución táctica de ciencia ficción, Zero Company le ofrece la solución.
